subject: Evaluation sprint & incentives for onramp
messages:
From: Maya Patel <maya@edgebank.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Peter Li <peter.li@edgebank.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Jan 2027 16:12:00 -0500
Subject: Evaluation sprint & incentives for onramp

Irene —

Thanks again for the demo earlier this week. We have internal approval to run a focused 6-week evaluation targeting ACH reconciliation and customer support triage. Before we start, procurement needs a short mutual action plan (MAP) showing milestones, acceptance gates, and any commercial incentives tied to those milestones.

High-level needs from our side:
- Week 1–2: data ingress and model access; success = secure test dataset loaded and baseline run
- Week 3–4: accuracy and workflows; success = F1 >= 0.78 on labeled set + two sample integrations
- Week 5–6: load and latency validation; success = 95th pctile < 350ms on staged traffic

Commercial asks we discussed with our CIO: pilot credits to offset engineering time, a one-time trial extension option if we need extra time for integration, and a clear conversion pricing path if we decide to go to production. Can you send a MAP that ties pilot credits and a conversion pricing ladder to the above milestones? Procurement also requested a simple attachments list and a copy of your SOC2 summary (we can accept a URL).

Attaching a terse draft MAP our PM put together: EdgeBank_MAP_Draft.xlsx (spreadsheet) — this is just to help format the milestones.

We're aiming to finish evaluation and have commercial terms for the board by the first week of February. Please let me know what you can commit to and any quick wins we can include to accelerate sign-off.

Best,
Maya Patel
Director, Product — EdgeBank
maya@edgebank.com
+1 (415) 555-0118

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Patel <maya@edgebank.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 25 Jan 2027 10:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Evaluation sprint & incentives for onramp

Hi Maya —

Appreciate the clear rundown — this is exactly the kind of MAP we like. I've sketched a proposal below that maps directly to your acceptance gates and includes a pragmatic incentive structure so we can align on close timing. Preview below; I'll send a formal MAP spreadsheet (MAP-template.xlsx) and SOC2 link once you confirm the rundown.

Proposed MAP summary (6-week sprint)
- Milestone 1 (Week 1–2): Data ingress + secure access. Deliverable: synced test dataset and baseline run. Incentive: $10k pilot credit on completion.
- Milestone 2 (Week 3–4): Accuracy & integration. Deliverable: labeled evaluation result with performance report (target F1 >= 0.78) and two integration demos. Incentive: $10k pilot credit on meeting quality gate.
- Milestone 3 (Week 5–6): Load & SLA test. Deliverable: performance report showing 95th pctile < 350ms. Incentive: $10k credit + option to apply remaining credit to first invoice on conversion.

Trial extension: one 2-week extension available by written request if integration blockers surface (extension consumes a portion of pilot credit unless we mutually agree to an exception).

Conversion pricing (at-signing tiers)
- 12-month commit: base price $0.0075 / token; 15% discount on month-1 list if annual upfront.
- 24-month commit: base price $0.0065 / token; 22% discount on month-1 list and 5% technical support credit.
- Flex (no commit): $0.009 / token, with standard rate-limited support.

Notes / gating items:
- Credits apply only to Redwood usage fees (not professional services or third-party costs).
- We require a signed MAP + PO for credits to be invoiced/allocated; credits will be applied over first two invoices unless parties agree otherwise.
- Standard commercial terms apply; legal can expedite a short MAP addendum for you.

Next steps:
1) Confirm the incentive amounts / whether the $30k total pilot credit is acceptable or if you need different structuring.
2) Share procurement contact and any required PO wording.
3) I'll loop Lauren for pricing paperwork and Rafael for final approval on the credit structure.

SOC2 summary: https://redwood.share/security/soc2-summary (public stub)

If that looks good I'll generate the formal MAP and a simple SOW addendum for the trial.

Thanks —
Irene Choi
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Evaluation sprint & incentives for onramp

Looping in a few commercial tweaks from my side. Overall I support the $30k total pilot credit but propose we structure it to protect Redwood while keeping EdgeBank comfortable. Suggested adjustments: 
- $25k applied as refundable trial credit (applies to usage invoices during the first 60 days); remaining $5k payable only upon signed PO converting to paid.
- If conversion occurs within 90 days of MAP-sign, apply an additional 5% conversion discount on the first three months (stackable with commit discount).
- If conversion is to a 24-mo commit, accelerate quota-based support (SLA uplift) as an incentive.

PO / legal ask: procurement often needs a one-page MSA addendum + a short billing contact and remit address. Use HubSpot deal for all docs: https://hubspot.company/DEAL-3271 (internal).

If Maya confirms, I'll get finance to pre-authorize credit allocation so we can hit your internal board timeline.

-Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Director, Commercial — Redwood Inference
rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
